The MRP is very simple, just this:

[testing.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19817110/testing.zip)

I saw a suggestion in another issue to use [get_instance_id](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_object.html#class-object-method-get-instance-id) as the key in typed dictionaries, so that's a potential workaround, but I imagine this is undesirable behaviour still.
I've also run into this issue.  I've switched several cases to use `get_instance_id` as the key as @suikanon notes, but it's not an ideal workaround as it involves extra steps on both set & get.

Below is my research on `4.5 Dev 3`(!).

I've dug a bit into the engine code and it seems, to my limited knowledge, that casting to a typed dictionary silently fails).
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1b4ed4c038c98bcfdc01337862a3a6954c616e62/core/io/marshalls.cpp#L1830
Below this point the keys of the dictionary seem to be "empty"? 
Iterating over `dict.values()` works without issues.
Iterating over `dict.keys()` works. `key.is_null()` is false. 

Using the key to get the value via `dict.getptr(key)` fails. 

On 4.5 Dev 3 even built-in classes seem to sort of fail in the inspector. The dictionary shows up in the inspector, the keys are shown (as object id) but the values are null (probably related to `dict.getptr(key)` failing, but why on built-in classes as well? Need to retest on 4.4.1-stable). This happens regardless of if the key-Node is in the tree or not (via add_child()).

Edit: I did a quick test of past 4.5 Dev builds:
(Hint: This regards built-in classes for now, will re-test with custom classes at a later time)
In Dev 1 and Dev 2: The inspector (remote tree) displays the dictionary without issues (keys as well as values) regardless of if the key is in the tree (add_child()).
In Dev 3 only the keys are displayed and values are `null`.  (Also regardless of if the key is the tree).


Considering this behaviour differs to custom classes (especially since custom classes are already having issues in 4.4.1) I think these are two separate issues (though they might be related to an extend).
